text: ← RETURN TO SELECTED WORK CASE STUDY 02 · VOICE AI COPILOT VOICE AI AGENT CONTROL OBSIDIAN NOTES Manas: Ciel — A Bilingual Voice Assistant for My Dev Workstation Ciel listens, answers in Japanese and English, hands tasks to my five LSFM agents, reads and writes my Obsidian notes, remembers the last 8 exchanges in each HUD tab, and speaks up when something on my PC needs attention. (The name comes from an anime character; the requirements came from my own workflow.) PROBLEM My working context is spread across the terminal, Discord, Obsidian notes and LLM chat tabs, and switching between them by hand breaks focus. CONSTRAINT One voice, in Japanese and English, running on my own PC, that can act on the workstation (hand tasks to the agents, read notes, check vitals) and not only chat. DECISION Speak each sentence as soon as it is written: Edge-TTS gets up to three sentences at once and the HUD plays them in order. Groq, Whisper and Ollama are called with Python's standard library, no SDK: HTTPS for Groq and Whisper, local HTTP for Ollama (decisions). MEASURED RESULT Time to first audio fell from 4.60 s to 1.41 s p50 (N=10 each, same prompt and machine, 2026-10-02). The cost: mission-complete p95 rose from 5.99 s to 7.20 s (before · after). TIME TO FIRST AUDIO 4.60 s → 1.41 s p50 · N = 10 each · 2026-10-02 Before streaming 4.60 s After streaming 1.41 s 0 s linear scale 6 s Each tick is one recorded run; the tall tick is the p50. Source: 2026-10-02-ttfa-before.json · 2026-10-02-ttfa-after.json CODE Server side in lsfm-ai-hq: speech_stream.py, ciel_server.py (the HUD code is private) ⚡ Try the Voice Demo ↓ See the 4 Parts ↓ View Code on GitHub ↗ PLATFORM Local Microservices · WebSockets · Chromium HUD · Obsidian Vault DISCIPLINE Voice AI & Multi-Agent Systems ROLE Developer & Systems Architect (Solo) STACK Python 3.11 (aiohttp) · Groq Whisper Turbo · Edge-TTS · FFmpeg DSP · Vanilla JS/CSS ● THE ENGINEERING CHALLENGE Siri, Alexa and ChatGPT Voice are built for everyone, so they can't see my code, my notes, or my running agents, and they forget everything between sessions. ● THE ARCHITECTURE SOLUTION Built Ciel as an async Python server: Groq Whisper Large v3 Turbo transcribes speech (OpenAI Whisper as fallback), Edge-TTS voices pass through a custom FFmpeg voice filter, and Ciel remembers the last 8 exchanges of each HUD tab separately, reads and writes my Obsidian notes, and runs background checks on my PC. 2-Tier SPEECH-TO-TEXT (GROQ → OPENAI) JA + EN BILINGUAL EDGE-TTS VOICES 8 Exchanges REMEMBERED, PLUS OBSIDIAN NOTES 5 Agents LSFM AGENTS CIEL CAN CALL Show the voice pipeline diagram TABLE OF CONTENTS 01. The Problem: Scattered Context 02. Design Decisions 03. What Broke & What I’d Change 04. Voice Demo 05. The 4 Parts of Manas: Ciel 06. How the Voice Sounds 07. Reading & Writing My Notes 08. Background Checks 09. Production Benchmarks // 01 · CONTEXT & PROBLEM The Problem: A Developer's Context Is Scattered Across Five Tools In modern software engineering, developers are bombarded by fragmentation: switching between terminal shells, Slack or Discord communication channels, Obsidian documentation vaults, and cloud LLM web interfaces. Rather than another generic chatbot, I built Manas: Ciel as one voice for all of it. Ciel works in two modes: answer general technical questions (algorithms, architecture, systems design), or act on my workstation: hand tasks to the five LSFM agents, check hardware vitals, and read the learned rules in my Obsidian notes. Design Stance: Ciel speaks as a calm, precise peer, not a servant: the system prompt rules out anime-style address such as "Master" or "マスター". // 02 · DESIGN DECISIONS Design Decisions & Their Costs Each card is one decision: what I chose, what I passed over, why, and what it costs. The evidence links point at the public code or result file at a pinned commit. ADR-CIEL-01 Standard-library HTTP calls for Groq, Whisper and Ollama; an SDK only for Gemini Decision Groq chat (including streaming), Groq and OpenAI Whisper, and local Ollama are called with Python's urllib. Gemini goes through Google's google-genai SDK. Alternatives The groq and openai Python SDKs for every provider. Why Groq and Whisper take simple JSON (or a multipart upload) over HTTPS, and Ollama takes the same JSON over plain HTTP on the local machine (127.0.0.1), so the same lightweight standard-library approach covers all three without an SDK, and the retry rules live in my code: Groq's fractional Retry-After (e.g. 1.5 s) is honoured once if it is 4 s or less, then the next model is tried. Cost Streaming, multipart uploads and 429 handling are hand-written, so each needs its own tests (GroqRetryAfterTest). Evidence llm_client.py · voice_engine.py ADR-CIEL-02 Speak each sentence as soon as it is written Decision Stream the synthesis reply and send each finished sentence to Edge-TTS (up to three requests at once); the HUD plays the clips in order. Alternatives Voice the whole reply after the LLM finishes (the 2026-10-01 design). Why Time to first audio fell from 4.60 s to 1.41 s p50 (N=10 each, 2026-10-02, same prompt and machine). Cost Mission-complete p95 rose from 5.99 s to 7.20 s: the joined replay MP3 waits for the slowest clip, and clips play strictly in order, so one slow clip holds back the sentences after it. Evidence before · after · speech_stream.py · ciel_orchestrator.py (clip queue, three at once, in order) ADR-CIEL-03 Push telemetry over the WebSocket instead of polling Decision The server pushes CPU, RAM and disk readings to connected HUDs every 5 s, and samples only while a client is connected. Alternatives The HUD polling an HTTP endpoint on a timer (how it worked before). Why Nothing is sampled or requested when no HUD is open, and the readings arrive on the WebSocket the HUD already holds for mission events. Cost The HUD needs reconnect logic with backoff, and still fetches one snapshot over HTTP when it (re)connects. Evidence ciel_server.py (5 s push, snapshot endpoint) · the HUD's reconnect and snapshot code is in hud.js, in a private repo // 03 · RETROSPECTIVE What Broke & What I Would Change ⚠️ What Broke in V1 Synchronous weather queries to wttr.in and live web search during voice generation caused the audio stream to block and stutter when the user had high internet latency. → The Fix (Shipped) Fixed, and the code is public in lsfm-ai-hq: every blocking call in a mission now runs in a worker thread via asyncio.to_thread: named mission tools (weather, web search, both LLM calls, psutil, Obsidian, git, Gmail, the PDF build) have per-call timeouts, while FFmpeg runs off the event loop without a timeout. The server's event loop keeps serving other clients while a mission waits. Independent agents run concurrently with asyncio.gather. A call that times out ends as an honest failed ("timed out after N s"), never an empty success. At most two missions run at once; a few more queue, and anything beyond that is refused with a 503 instead of flooding the thread pool. Regression tests prove the loop keeps ticking while a tool blocks. 🛠️ Production Architecture Note While edge-tts needs no API key and returned an English clip in 0.42 s p50 in the 2026-10-01 bench (a network round trip to Microsoft's service), enterprise production deployment would swap it for self-hosted Kokoro/Vits pipelines or dedicated WebRTC audio streaming to satisfy enterprise uptime SLAs. // 04 · SCRIPTED HUD DEMO Voice Demo: What Ciel Can Do A scripted demo of Ciel's replies. Click any prompt chip to see the kind of response Ciel gives. Replies are pre-written examples, not live output: MANAS: CIEL HUD SCRIPTED DEMO · PRE-WRITTEN REPLIES VOICE FILTER: ON VOICE QUERY: 👥 5-Agent System Status 🌤️ Live Weather (wttr.in) 🌐 Web Search (DDGS) 🧠 General Knowledge (Raft) 📜 Obsidian Learned Rules 🎯 Working Preferences ⚡ Hardware & Vitals 🚀 Dispatch Sakura ⚡ AUDIO PIPELINE: FFMPEG 16 KHZ MONO + VOICE-BAND FILTER → GROQ WHISPER TURBO → EDGE-TTS + VOICE FILTER [CIEL · SAMPLE REPLY] Delegating to the 5-agent team. Eunchae reports CPU, RAM and disk use; Yunjin scans the portfolio for broken assets; Kazuha lists the current branch and uncommitted files; Sakura pulls today's priorities from the daily log. Summary compiled for you. The live HUD gets these steps from ciel_server.py over a WebSocket at /ws, as they happen: plan_formed when Ciel has a plan, agent_state for each agent it delegates to, ciel_audio_chunk for each spoken clip, then ciel_complete or ciel_error. CPU and RAM are pushed every 5 s. Each tab has its own session id, so a mission's events reach only the tab that asked, and the HUD's stamp shows how the plan was made (by the LLM, by a keyword fast path, or by a fallback). The HUD's own browser tests replay these events against a faked server in CI. // 05 · ARCHITECTURAL FOUNDATION The 4 Parts of Manas: Ciel Ciel has four parts: agent control, memory and notes, speech, and background checks. ⚡ PILLAR 01 · ORCHESTRATION Agent Control Ciel hands tasks to the five LSFM agents (Sakura, Chaewon, Kazuha, Yunjin, Eunchae) and collects their results, so I don't have to switch to Discord. lsfm-ai-hq · ciel_orchestrator.py 🧠 PILLAR 02 · KNOWLEDGE Memory & Obsidian Notes Remembers the last 8 exchanges per HUD tab (up to 16 tabs; the least recently used is forgotten first), checks live weather (`wttr.in`) and the web (`ddgs`), and reads and writes my Obsidian notes (`ciel_read_rules`, `ciel_read_profile`, `ciel_search_vault`, `ciel_save_to_daily`). Last 8 Exchanges · wttr.in · DDGS · Obsidian 🎙️ PILLAR 03 · SPEECH DSP Clean Audio In, Clear Voice Out FFmpeg conversion to 16 kHz mono with a voice-band filter, Groq Whisper Large v3 Turbo with domain vocabulary prompting, an OpenAI Whisper fallback, and live Web Audio ring reactivity. Groq Whisper Turbo · Edge-TTS DSP 🛡️ PILLAR 04 · TELEMETRY Background Checks Background loop running 4 checks every 45 seconds: hardware CPU/RAM/disk, Git status, today's Obsidian daily log, and portfolio TODO markers. Pushes the top 3 suggestions to the HUD over WebSockets. proactive_sentinel.py · WebSockets // 06 · SIGNAL PROCESSING & DSP How the Voice Sounds: Audio Cleanup & Voice Filter Plain text-to-speech sounds flat. To give Ciel a calm, close presence, the pipeline has two FFmpeg stages, one on the way in and one on the way out: Inbound (speech-to-text prep), piped in memory: ffmpeg -i pipe:0 -ar 16000 -ac 1 -af "volume=1.8,highpass=f=80,lowpass=f=7500" -f wav pipe:1 Outbound (voice filter over the JA + EN Edge-TTS clips): [0:a]apad=pad_dur=0.35[a0];[a0][1:a]concat=n=2:v=0:a=1,highpass=f=120,equalizer=f=3500:t=q:w=1.2:g=3.0,aecho=0.85:0.8:25|45:0.18|0.09,volume=0.30 Engineering rationale for these parameters: 16 kHz Mono Conversion: Whisper models are trained on 16,000 Hz single-channel audio. Converting the browser's WebM/Opus recording through stdin/stdout pipes avoids temp files and container ambiguity, and the 80 Hz–7.5 kHz band-pass trims rumble and hiss before transcription. Bilingual Sequencing: The Japanese line plays first, then a 350 ms pause, then the English line, so the two voices read as one deliberate utterance rather than an overlap. Presence, Not Speed: A 120 Hz high-pass removes room boom and a +3 dB lift at 3.5 kHz adds clarity. The voices themselves are tuned slightly lower and slower (−2 to −3 Hz pitch, −1 to −2% rate) for a calm delivery. "Inside the Mind" Echo: Two faint reflections at 25 ms and 45 ms create the sense of an internal thought rather than an external loudspeaker, without the smear of a full reverb. Bounded Audio Cache: Rendered replies are kept in audio_cache/; on server start-up only the 35 most recent files are kept, so the cache can't grow without bound. // 07 · READ & WRITE NOTES Ciel Reads and Writes My Obsidian Notes Most voice assistants can't see your notes. Ciel reads and writes my Obsidian vault through Obsidian's Local REST API, and falls back to reading the files on disk: Show the vault tool definitions When Hans asks: "What are my working preferences?" or "Remind me of the rule regarding edge redirect syntax," Ciel picks the matching tool, reads the note, and answers from it. If Obsidian's REST plugin is off, it reads the file from disk instead, so the request still succeeds. // 08 · BACKGROUND CHECKS Background Checks: Ciel Speaks Up First Passive voice assistants only speak when spoken to. Ciel runs a background-check loop (proactive_sentinel.py) every 45 seconds while the HUD is connected, ranks what it finds (warning > action > info), and surfaces the top 3 across 4 checks: ⚡ Hardware Check Reads psutil vitals and warns when CPU load passes 85%, RAM passes 88%, or drive C: drops under 20 GB free. Each warning offers a one-click hand-off to Eunchae. 🗓️ Daily Log Check Opens today's Obsidian daily log. If it's missing, Ciel suggests Sakura's briefing; otherwise it routes the first unchecked priority to the matching agent by keyword. 📄 Portfolio Check Scans the portfolio's index.html for leftover TODO or FIXME markers and offers a Yunjin audit. 🐙 Git Check Runs git status --porcelain on the workspace and, at 3 or more uncommitted changes, offers a Kazuha review of the diff. When an anomaly is flagged, Ciel displays an advisory telemetry badge on the Voice HUD (e.g. ✦ 2 ADVISORY) and emits a non-intrusive notification toast allowing one-click resolution. // 09 · PIPELINE STAGES & TIMINGS Pipeline Stages & Measured Timings 1 · HUD Push-to-talk WebM upload, or a typed prompt 2 · Transcribe FFmpeg 16 kHz mono → Groq Whisper (OpenAI fallback) 3 · Admit 2 missions run, 8 wait, the rest get a 503 4 · Route Keyword fast paths, else a Groq JSON plan 5 · Tools & agents Threads with timeouts; PDF & Gmail get their own pool 6 · Synthesize (streaming) Groq writes the JA line, the EN line, then the report 7 · Speak while writing Each finished sentence → Edge-TTS + filter → HUD 8 · Complete Report + joined MP3 for replay, or ciel_error One voice request, end to end. Stage timings are in the tables below, with their run counts and dates. Every voice turn runs through these stages on my workstation (Intel Core i5-12400F, 16GB DDR4, AMD Radeon RX 6600 XT, Windows 11). The p50 column comes from bench/bench_ciel.py in the public repo: N = 10 runs per stage on 2026-10-01 (full results, including p95 and max: bench/results/2026-10-01.md). Network stages are round trips from this machine at that time, not compute times. A full mission for a general-knowledge prompt (routing, synthesis and bilingual speech) took 4.43 s p50 (max 5.71 s). PIPELINE STAGE ENGINE WHAT HAPPENS P50 (N=10) Audio Conversion FFmpeg Resample to 16 kHz mono WAV with a fixed gain (×1.8) and an 80 Hz–7.5 kHz band-pass. 32 ms Speech-to-Text Groq Whisper Large v3 Turbo → OpenAI whisper-1 Domain-vocabulary prompt; the OpenAI tier runs only if Groq fails. 0.50 s · network Intent Routing Keyword pre-router + Groq qwen3.8-27b Fast paths for weather, search, and memory reset; the LLM returns a JSON plan for everything else. 0.58 s · network Tools & Agents wttr.in · DDGS · Obsidian REST · 5 LSFM agents Runs the planned tools in worker threads with per-call timeouts; delegated agents run concurrently. Per tool: vitals 0.50 s, web search 4.6 s · network Synthesis Groq qwen3.8-27b Writes the full report plus short Japanese and English lines to speak. 0.96 s · network Voice Edge-TTS + FFmpeg filter Japanese clip, a 350 ms pause, then the English clip, filtered off the event loop in worker threads (no timeout). In this 2026-10-01 run the full MP3 was rendered before playback; streaming is below. 2.80 s · network (filter alone 81 ms) Streaming Speech: Time to First Audio The table above shows the cost: no sound until the whole reply had been voiced. Ciel now streams the synthesis reply and voices each spoken sentence as soon as the LLM finishes writing it (up to three Edge-TTS requests at once). The HUD plays the clips in order while the rest is still being generated. Time to first audio runs from the start of the mission until the first playable audio URL is broadcast to the HUD; the HUD's fetch of a local file comes on top. FULL MISSION, N=10 EACH BEFORE (WHOLE REPLY) AFTER (PER SENTENCE) Time to first audio, p50 / p95 4.60 s / 5.99 s 1.41 s / 2.00 s Mission complete, p50 / p95 4.60 s / 5.99 s 4.29 s / 7.20 s Measured 2026-10-02 with bench/bench_ciel.py --stages e2e_mission --runs 10: the same general-knowledge prompt, Groq paced 45 s between runs, on an Intel Core i5-12400F, Windows 11, Python 3.11.9, ffmpeg 9.0.2, edge-tts 7.2.8. Network round trips from this machine, not compute times; with 10 runs, p95 is the max. Code: LE-SSERAFIM-AI-HQ 3315b69 (before) and 3eedda9 (after), public in lsfm-ai-hq since 14a319f (speech_stream.py). Full results: ttfa-before.md, ttfa-after.md. The trade-off is in the second row. The first sentence is heard about 3.2 s sooner at p50, but the joined MP3 kept for replay waits for the slowest clip. In one of the ten runs a single Edge-TTS clip took 6.2 s, which set the 7.20 s worst case. Clips play strictly in order, so a slow clip also holds back the sentences after it; the pauses this causes between sentences are not measured yet. One Recorded Mission, Call by Call The tables above pool many runs. This is a single mission as it happened: the median of 10 runs (3.14 s end to end), with each timed call drawn at its recorded start and end. First audio was ready at 1.25 s, while the synthesis LLM was still writing. First audio at 1.25 s; mission complete at 3.14 s.
